This module runs automated data-quality checks (outliers, miscoded missing values, empty and constant columns, SPSS filter variables, category casing, problematic column names, mixed text encodings, spreadsheet formatting) on the extracted data files.
We examined 21 columns across 4 data files.
3 file/column combinations have at least one issue.

```{r} #| echo: false # table data -------------------------------------- table <- structure(list(File = c("dupnames.csv", "types.csv", "types.csv" ), Column = c("x", "mixed", "txt"), Issues = c("👥 Colliding column names — Column name becomes \"x\" when special characters are replaced, the s...", "#️⃣ Numeric as text — Column is 80% numeric but 1 value cannot be parsed: \"a\"", "🔤 Case issues — Categories differing only by case: Apple/apple" )), row.names = c(NA, -3L), class = "data.frame") # display table ----------------------------------- metacheck::report_table(table, "auto", 20, FALSE) ```
No file could be screened for careless responding.

**What this does not cover.** Only 0 of 4 data files could be screened: the rest had no detectable multi-item scale block, or too few respondents. Even in a screened file, these checks only look at multi-item rating scales — the only place where a repeated or flat answer pattern is interpretable. Single questions, open text, demographics and any item outside a detected scale block are never examined. A respondent can therefore answer most of a survey carelessly and still not be flagged here, and finding nothing is not evidence that a dataset is free of careless responding.

-  We classified 5 files: 5 data.
-  We found 5 tabular data files and extracted 21 columns from 4 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1).
-  The study-group step did not get an answer for 5 files (the model request failed); they were grouped by the fallback rules instead.
-  1 file read as a table but is not a usable rectangular dataset (headeronly.csv: the file has no data rows or columns). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: headeronly.csv. We ran automated data-quality checks on 21 columns; 3 columns have at least one potential issue (1 column with inconsistent category casing; 1 column whose names become identical when special characters are removed; 1 column with numeric values stored as text).

Column name becomes "x" when special characters are replaced, the same as 1 other identically named column: tools that sanitize names (R's make.names(), SPSS/SAS/Stata import, codebook section links) cannot tell these columns apart.
